insurer: Aditya Birla Health Insurance Co. Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (as per Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table)

great.name: Restore/Reload Benefit (unrelated illness only) available once per policy year
great.quote: Once in the Policy Year, We shall provide for a reload of the Sum Insured... Reload of Sum Insured shall be available only once during a Policy Year... (iii) The reload of Sum Insured shall be available only for subsequent claims and not in relation to any Illness/ Injury (including its complications) for which a claim has been admitted for the Insured Person during that Policy Year.
great.reference: Section C.I.(h) Reload of Sum Insured
great.explanation: This replenishes your Sum Insured (once a year) after it becomes insufficient due to earlier claims, but it cannot be used for the same illness/complications already claimed in that policy year. As per your rules, restore that works only for unrelated illnesses is still a strong feature vs policies with no restore at all.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days (standard)
good.quote: 30-day waiting period (Code- Excl03) i. Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Non-accident illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days; accidents are typically exempt. This is standard in health insurance.

good.name: Specific illness/procedure waiting period: 24 months (standard)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with Us.
good.explanation: Listed diseases/surgeries are covered only after 24 months unless due to an accident. This is industry-standard (not a red flag).

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: present but day-limit as per schedule
good.quote: We shall cover on a reimbursement basis, up to the Sum Insured for the number of days in accordance with the limit as speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule / Product Beneﬁt Table of this Policy, the Insured Person’s Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization expenses are covered, but the number of days is not stated in this excerpt and depends on your plan/schedule.

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: present but day-limit as per schedule
good.quote: We shall cover on a reimbursement basis, up to the Sum Insured for the number of days speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule / Product Beneﬁt Table of this Policy, the Insured Person’s Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization expenses are covered, but the number of days is plan/schedule-dependent in this excerpt.

good.name: No Claim Bonus (NCB): up to 50% with partial reduction on claim (does not reset to zero)
good.quote: The accumulated No Claim Bonus shall not exceed 50% of the Sum Insured on the Renewed Policy. In the event of a claim impacting the eligibility of a No Claim Bonus, the accumulated No Claim Bonus shall be reduced by 10% of the Sum Insured at the commencement of subsequent Policy Year.
good.explanation: Your Sum Insured can grow up to 50% if claim-free. If a claim happens, NCB reduces by 10% of SI rather than dropping to zero, which is better than many market NCB designs.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization (Home Care): covered (with conditions)
good.quote: We shall cover the Medical Expenses incurred for the Insured Person’s Domiciliary Hospitalization, up to the limits as speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule / Product Beneﬁt Table of this Policy
good.explanation: Home treatment is covered when medically necessary (e.g., patient cannot be shifted or bed not available), subject to conditions and some listed illnesses not covered under this benefit.

bad.name: Room rent limit applies (not at actuals); proportionate/rateable deductions apply if you take a higher room category
bad.quote: Reasonable and Customary Charges for Room Rent... up to the limits as speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule / Product Beneﬁt Table of this Policy; ... If the Insured Person is admitted in a room category/limit that is higher than the one that is speciﬁed... then the Insured Person shall bear a rateable proportion of the total Associated Medical Expenses
bad.reference: Section C.I.(a) In-patient Hospitalization (Room rent) + Conditions (2)
bad.explanation: Because room rent is limited as per schedule (not ‘any room/no limit’ in the default wording), choosing a higher room category can trigger proportionate deductions on several associated hospital costs, increasing out-of-pocket expenses.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (non-medical consumables like gloves, masks, kits etc. excluded via Non-medical list)
bad.quote: Non-Medical Expenses... as speciﬁed in the Annexure I - Non- Medical Expenses... List I - Items for which coverage is not available in the policy... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 58 ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]
bad.reference: Section D.II.(50) + Annexure I (Non-medical expenses list)
bad.explanation: Many day-to-day hospital consumables and non-medical items can be billed separately and are excluded, creating out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization.

bad.name: No restore benefit beyond reload; reload is restricted (not same illness in same policy year; not for first claim)
bad.quote: (ii) The reload of Sum Insured shall not apply to the ﬁrst claim in the Policy Year. (iii) The reload of Sum Insured shall be available only for subsequent claims and not in relation to any Illness/ Injury (including its complications) for which a claim has been admitted for the Insured Person during that Policy Year.
bad.reference: Section C.I.(h) Reload of Sum Insured
bad.explanation: While reload exists, it is limited: it won’t help on the first claim and won’t help for the same illness/complications again in that year. If you need a restore that works for same illness too, this may be insufficient.

unclear.name: Co-pay amount for age 61+ (mandatory) not specified in wording excerpt (depends on schedule)
unclear.quote: At the time of inception... if the Age... is 61 years or above... shall bear a Co-payment per claim... as speciﬁed in Product Beneﬁt Table/Policy Schedule.
unclear.explanation: Co-pay definitely applies for entry age 61+ (mandatory), but the exact percentage is not given here. Check your Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table.

unclear.name: PED (Pre-existing disease) waiting period duration not specified (depends on schedule)
unclear.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of years / months as speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule / Product Beneﬁt Table of this Policy
unclear.explanation: The PED waiting period is not stated in this excerpt and must be confirmed from the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table.

unclear.name: Pre-hospitalization days limit not specified (schedule-based)
unclear.quote: for the number of days in accordance with the limit as speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule / Product Beneﬁt Table of this Policy
unclear.explanation: The feature exists, but the exact number of covered days is not visible here; it varies by plan.

unclear.name: Post-hospitalization days limit not specified (schedule-based)
unclear.quote: for the number of days speciﬁed in the Policy Schedule / Product Beneﬁt Table of this Policy
unclear.explanation: The feature exists, but the exact number of covered days is not visible here; it varies by plan.
